text:
Damon Severson is having the kind of season where the points look fine and the details tell a more complicated story. He has 2 goals and 6 assists in 18 games for Columbus, but his ice time over the last ten games is down 3.75 minutes from his season average, to about 20 a night.

The luck has run in his favor. Columbus has scored 7.2 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, one of the bigger gaps on this list, and his shooting percentage of 14.3% is more than twice the league rate for defensemen. Neither is likely to last.

Underneath, there is a good player. Evolving-Hockey ranked him 20th among 215 defensemen last season, with his team creating more and allowing less with him on the ice than nearly any defenseman. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a setup man: 6.1 primary shot assists per 60, 88th percentile at his position. At five-on-five this season Columbus is close to even with him on, 49% of the expected goals. Watch the minutes. If they keep sliding while the bounces cool, the points will follow them down.
headline: Riding the bounces, losing minutes
